rules: When an instruction is encoded as masked (vm=0), vector merge instructions combine the first operand to the destination element if the mask value is zero, otherwise they copy the second operand to the destination element.
When an instruction is encoded as masked (vm=0), vector integer add/subtract instructions operate on and write back all body elements.
When an instruction is encoded as masked (vm=0), vector integer multiply-add instructions operate on and write back all body elements.
Vector integer move instructions are encoded as unmasked instructions (vm=1).
Vector integer move instructions copy a source operand to a vector register group.
Vector integer move instructions splat a scalar register or immediate to all active elements of the destination vector register group.
Vector integer compare instructions write 1 to the destination mask register element if the comparison evaluates to true, and 0 otherwise.
Vector floating-point compare instructions raise the invalid operation exception only on signaling NaN inputs.
Vector floating-point compare instructions raise the invalid operation exception on both signaling and quiet NaN inputs.
Vector floating-point instructions that modify any floating-point extension state must set mstatus.FS to Dirty.
Vector single-width saturating add and subtract instructions set the vxsat bit if the result would overflow the destination.
Vector averaging add and subtract instructions ignore overflow for subtraction and the result wraps around.
Vector single-width fractional multiply instructions set the vxsat bit if the result causes saturation.
Vector single-width scaling shift instructions round off the shifted out bits according to the vxrm CSR.
Vector narrowing clip instructions use the rounding mode specified in the vxrm CSR.
When performing a narrowing unsigned clip, the shifted rounded source value is treated as an unsigned integer and saturates if the result would overflow the destination viewed as an unsigned integer.
When performing a narrowing signed clip, the shifted rounded source value is treated as a signed integer and saturates if the result would overflow the destination viewed as a signed integer.
Vector ordered single-width floating-point sum reduction performs the computation: vd[0] = (((vs1[0] + vs2[0]) + vs2[1]) + ...) + vs2[vl-1].
When performing a masked ordered floating-point sum reduction, masked-off elements do not affect the result or the exception flags.
When performing an unordered single-width floating-point sum reduction, the implementation computes an exact sum using infinite precision before converting to a floating-point format.
When performing an unordered single-width floating-point sum reduction, the reduction tree structure must be deterministic for a given value in vtype and vl.
When performing an unordered single-width floating-point sum reduction, the additive identity is +0.0 when rounding down (towards -∞) or -0.0 for all other rounding modes.
Vector widening integer reduction instructions perform overflows by wrapping around.

Vector widening unsigned integer reduction instructions zero-extend the SEW-wide vector elements before summing them and add the 2*SEW-width scalar element, storing the result in a 2*SEW-width scalar element.

Vector widening signed integer reduction instructions sign-extend the SEW-wide vector elements before summing them and add the 2*SEW-width scalar element, storing the result in a 2*SEW-width scalar element.

Vector widening floating-point reduction instructions perform the SEW-width element reduction as in the single-width case, with elements in vs2 promoted to 2*SEW bits before adding to the 2*SEW-bit accumulator.
